# Hardware access

The Frame is built on a Qualcomm SM8650 (`/sys/devices/soc0/machine` reports a string of the form `SM8650 <board revision> 4slam 2et`). Most hardware is reachable through ordinary Linux interfaces: hwmon, IIO, LED class devices, V4L2 and spidev. The trick is knowing which node is which. Valve ships a small helper for exactly that.

The `steamos` user is in the `video`, `render`, `input`, `audio`, `leds`, `cdsp`, `spidev`, `perf`, `gpiod` and `fpga` groups (plus `wheel`; see [permissions](permissions.md)). Udev rules in `/usr/lib/udev/rules.d/99-*.rules` give those groups access to the matching device nodes, so a lot of this works without root.

Unless a section says otherwise, everything on this page is **Internal**: plain Linux interfaces, but the specific paths and helpers are Valve's and can change.

## `vrdevice_path`: the name-to-node map

**Tag: Internal.** Valve's battery, codec and FPGA scripts call this helper to find hardware. `/usr/local/bin/vrdevice_path <key>` prints the device node or sysfs file for a named piece of hardware, and many of Valve's other helpers are one-line wrappers around it. Run it with no arguments to list the keys. Paths as resolved on the headset surveyed:

| Key | Path |
|---|---|
| `model` | Board stage string from the EEPROM. `fpga_load.sh` checks it for `EV1` and `Unknown`. Prints a value, not a path. |
| `board_revision`, `minor_revision` | Board revision values from the EEPROM |
| `imu` | `/dev/imu` |
| `imu_raw` | `/dev/spidev20.0` |
| `cdsp`, `adsp` | `/dev/cdsp` |
| `camera_left` / `camera_control_left` | `/dev/video1` / `/dev/v4l-subdev15` |
| `camera_right` / `camera_control_right` | `/dev/video2` / `/dev/v4l-subdev14` |
| `camera_names` | `passthrough_right passthrough_left slam_left slam_right upper_left upper_right` |
| `camera_v4l_subdev <name>` | `/dev/v4l-subdev28`–`33`, in the order above |
| `video_encode` / `video_decode` | `/dev/video23` / `/dev/video22` (hardware codec) |
| `prox_sensor` | `/sys/bus/iio/devices/iio:device2/in_proximity_raw` |
| `battery_voltage_now` | `/sys/bus/iio/devices/iio:device0/in_voltage_pm8550b_vbat_sns_chgr_input` |
| `battery_current_now` | `/sys/bus/iio/devices/iio:device0/in_current_pm8550b_ichg_fb_input` |
| `battery_power_now`, `battery_power_avg`, `battery_power_avg_recent` | `/sys/bus/iio/devices/iio:device1/power_*` |
| `battery_avg_start`, `battery_avg_stop`, `battery_avg_running` | `/sys/bus/iio/devices/iio:device1/{start,stop,timer_state}` |
| `battery_capacity` | `/run/deckardcharger/battery_percent` |
| `usb_voltage`, `usb_current` | IIO channels on `iio:device0` |
| `usb_charger_online`, `usb_charger_type` | Type-C port power supply (`tcpm-source-psy-…`) |
| `pon_reason` | PMIC power-on reason |
| `fpga_spidev` | `/dev/spidev1.0` |
| `display_panel` | `/sys/bus/mipi-dsi/devices/ae94000.dsi.0` |
| `display_dsi` | `/sys/kernel/debug/dri/ae01000.display-controller/DSI-1/panel` |
| `scene_illum_ir_led` | `/sys/class/leds/mp3317-scene-illum-ir` |
| `eeprom` | `/usr/lib/deckard-eeprom/eeprom_console` |

Some quirks:

- The script doesn't check whether a path exists. `imu` (`/dev/imu`) and `imu_raw` (`/dev/spidev20.0`) can point at nodes that aren't present, so check before opening anything.
- The key for camera interfaces is spelled `camera_inferface` in the script, and it returned "Unknown device" for every camera.
- `cdsp` and `adsp` both resolve to `/dev/cdsp`. That's what the script returns, not a typo here.
- `eeprom` returns the path of a tool, not a device.

## Battery and charging

### Helper commands

**Tag: Internal.** All of these are short shell scripts in `/usr/bin` that print a number:

| Command | Unit |
|---|---|
| `battery_capacity` | percent |
| `battery_voltage` | mV |
| `battery_current` | mA |
| `battery_power` | mW (voltage × current) |
| `battery_power_avg`, `battery_power_avg_recent` | from the averaging IIO device |
| `battery_power_avg_now` | starts averaging, waits 250 ms, prints, stops |
| `battery_avg_start` / `battery_avg_stop` / `battery_avg_running` | control the averaging timer (start/stop need write access) |
| `battery_delta` | the value of `…/typec@2b00/balancing/delta`, or "missing driver" if that file doesn't exist |
| `battery_charger_type` | USB charger type |
| `usb_voltage`, `usb_current` | mV, mA at the USB-C input |

### `/run/deckardcharger/`

**Tag: Internal.** `deckard_charge_daemon` (root) publishes a summary here that other services read. It's the simplest way to get charge state:

| File | Example |
|---|---|
| `battery_percent` | Percent, with one decimal place |
| `battery_status` | `Full`, `Charging`, `Discharging`, … |
| `ac_status` | Whether external power is connected (e.g. `Connected`) |
| `typec_contract` | USB-PD contract, as `Valid=<0\|1>, Voltage=<mV>mV, Current=<mA>mA` |
| `secs_until_battery_full` | Seconds |
| `secs_until_shutdown_request` | Seconds |
| `power_event` | |
| `vr_state` | e.g. `Running`. Owned by `steamos`; `ledcontrol` chowns it (its strings include `Could not chown /run/deckardcharger/vr_state`). |
| `BAT0` | symlink to `/sys/class/power_supply/max1720x_bat_7-36/` |

## Status LED

**Tag: Internal.** The RGB status LED is `/sys/class/leds/rgb:status` (a multicolor LED with `multi_intensity` and `hw_pattern`). `deckard-led-control.service` runs `/usr/bin/ledcontrol` as root. It watches `/run/deckardcharger/` with inotify, listens to logind for suspend/resume, and picks a color from this set:

```
OFF  WHITE  DIM_WHITE  BRIGHT_WHITE  WHITE_THROB
DIM_GREEN  YELLOW  BRIGHT_YELLOW  YELLOW_THROB  RED
```

The `leds` group can write every LED class device, so you can drive the LED yourself, but `ledcontrol` sets it again whenever the files in `/run/deckardcharger/` change. **Don't run `/usr/bin/ledcontrol` by hand.** It ignores arguments and starts a second copy of the daemon (see [methodology](methodology.md#incident-running-unknown-binaries-with---help)).

How charge state reaches the LED:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    accTitle: How charge state reaches the status LED
    accDescr: deckard_charge_daemon (root) writes /run/deckardcharger/, which other services read. ledcontrol (root) watches it with inotify and also gets suspend/resume events from logind, and sets the color of /sys/class/leds/rgb:status. A manual write by the leds group also reaches the LED but is overwritten by ledcontrol when /run/deckardcharger/ changes.
    CD["deckard_charge_daemon<br/>(root)"] -->|"writes"| RD["/run/deckardcharger/"]
    RD -->|"read by"| O["other services"]
    RD -->|"inotify"| LC["ledcontrol (root)"]
    LG["logind"] -->|"suspend/resume events"| LC
    LC -->|"sets color"| LED["/sys/class/leds/rgb:status"]
    U["manual write<br/>(leds group)"] -->|"overwritten by<br/>ledcontrol when<br/>/run/deckardcharger/<br/>changes"| LED
```

Other LED class devices: `mp3317-backlight-left`, `mp3317-backlight-right` and `mp3317-scene-illum-ir` (`vrdevice_path scene_illum_ir_led` points at the last one).

## Power rails

**Tag: Internal.** Three MAX34417 power monitors are exposed through hwmon, each with four channels:

| hwmon name | Channels |
|---|---|
| `max34417_9_12` | `apc0`, `apc2`, `apc1`, `nsp1` |
| `max34417_9_1a` | `gfx`, `nsp2`, `bob`, `unused` |
| `max34417_9_10` | `vph`, `s1c`, `s3c`, `s6c` |

The comments in Valve's `power_rail_monitor` describe these as Kryo APC0–2 cores, Tensor Processor NSP1/NSP2, GFX power, VPH power, BOB, and the S1C/S3C/S6C sub-regulation rails.

```bash
for h in /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*; do
  case "$(cat $h/name)" in max34417*)
    paste <(cat $h/power*_label) <(cat $h/power*_input) ;;
  esac
done
```

`power_rail_monitor` (Python) does this with nicer names. Its comments list separate channel orders for boards labeled EV2 and EV3. `measurement_mode` on each device is writable by the `perf` group. `deckard_power_monitor` (root, every 2 s) is the system's own logger.

## Thermals and the fan

There are about 55 hwmon devices. Most are SoC thermal zones (`cpu*_thermal`, `gpuss_*_thermal`, `nsp*_thermal`, `ddr_thermal`, `camera*_thermal`, PMIC temperatures). IIO device 0 also has temperature channels named `in_temp_pcba_at_fan_exhaust_input`, `…_at_heat_sink_fins_input`, `…_at_wifi_input`, `…_at_flash_input` and `…_at_40pin_connector_input`.

The fan is on hwmon device `slg4ax46073v` (`fan1_input`, `pwm1`, `pwm1_enable`). `/usr/bin/fanspeed` is a small tool for it:

```sh
fanspeed -p        # print RPM and PWM
sudo fanspeed -s 50   # fixed duty cycle in percent, 0–100 (pwm1 is root-only)
```

The control loop is `deckard-fan-control.service` (`/usr/share/deckard-fan-control/fancontrol.py`, root). Its config, `deckard-config.yaml`, sets `fan_min_speed: 30`, `fan_charging_min_speed: 40`, `fan_max_speed: 55` and `fan_min_time_on: 90`, plus `A/B/C_quad_control` and `A/B_ff_control` coefficients. Its first `devices` entry is `cpu7_middle_thermal` (`type: ffquad`, `T_threshold: 45`, `max_temp: 95`).

Thermal zones, trip points and cooling devices are on [power → thermal zones](power.md#thermal-zones).

To set the PWM yourself, stop the daemon first with `sudo systemctl stop deckard-fan-control`, and start it again when you're done. The daemon writes `pwm1` on every control cycle (`fancontrol.py`), so a manual setting won't hold while it runs.

## Cameras

Six cameras show up as V4L2 sub-devices, named by `vrdevice_path camera_names`: `passthrough_left`, `passthrough_right`, `slam_left`, `slam_right`, `upper_left` and `upper_right`. No eye-tracking camera appears as a V4L2 or I²C device. `dsp_service`'s journal tags aDSP camera messages `[OV6211]` (`Bringing cameras out of reset`, `Starting streaming.`), as part of the eye-tracking pipeline ([OpenXR → eye tracking](openxr.md#eye-tracking-foveation-hands-and-passthrough)).

A bound driver doesn't mean a working sensor. At boot the `og01a1b` and `og0ve10` drivers log `…_set_power_on: failed to enable power` and `Failed to get chip ID for <camera>`, yet all four stay bound and their `v4l-subdev` nodes exist ([kernel → boot-time quirks](kernel.md#boot-time-quirks)). Check `dmesg` before assuming a sub-device has a sensor answering behind it.

While SteamVR runs, `XRService` holds `/dev/media0`, the sub-devices for `passthrough_left` and the four `slam_*`/`upper_*` cameras, and several `/dev/video*` capture nodes. `v4l2cam` holds `/dev/video99`, and `steamwebhelper` holds the hardware decoder node `/dev/video22`.

`/dev/video99` is a v4l2loopback device (`modprobe v4l2loopback video_nr=99 card_label=SteamVR exclusive_caps=1` in `steamvr-v4l2loopback.service`). It's listed as "SteamVR" in `v4l2-ctl --list-devices`, is readable by the `video` group, and is held open by `v4l2cam` (`--output=99`). What it carries wasn't captured.

## Other sensors

| Sensor | Where |
|---|---|
| Proximity (Vishay VCNL4040, `vcnl4000` driver) | IIO `iio:device2`, `in_proximity_raw`. `prox_sensor_val` prints it. No process holds the IIO device node open; read it through sysfs. What reads it is on [power → proximity sensor](power.md#proximity-sensor). |
| Hall sensor (ALS31300) | input device `als31300` (an evdev `/dev/input/event*` node plus a joystick node). SteamVR's CV driver searches `/dev/input/event*` for a device named `als31300` in its `CHmdDirectDeviceControl` code. What it measures isn't stated. |
| Buttons | input devices `gpio-keys`, `pmic_pwrkey`, `pmic_resin` |
| PMIC ADC | IIO `iio:device0`. Voltages, currents and board temperatures. |

## FPGA

**Tag: Internal.** `deckard-fpga.service` loads a bitstream at boot (`/usr/lib/deckard-fpga/fpga_load.sh`), and `deckard-fpga-resume.service` reloads it after suspend ([services](services.md#hardware-and-power)). The FPGA is reached over `/dev/spidev1.0` (the `fpga_spidev` key in `vrdevice_path`) and programmed with a tool called `littlebee_config`.

`/usr/lib/deckard-fpga/images/` has five bitstreams, and each contains the strings `GW1N-2`, `GW1N-2C-WLCSP100H` and `GW1N-LV2CS100HC7`:

| File | Selected by `fpga_load.sh` when |
|---|---|
| `csi_agg_deckard_ev1_1_<variant>.binx` | `vrdevice_path model` is `EV1` with `minor_revision` 1, or any model other than `EV1`/`Unknown` |
| `csi_agg_deckard_ev1_<variant>.binx` | `model` is `EV1` with another minor revision |
| `csi_agg_dev_passthru.binx` | never referenced by the script |

`<variant>` is `passthru` by default, or `vcint` when the script is run as `fpga_load.sh VCINT`. The loader logs which one it loads (`journalctl -u deckard-fpga`): "Loading passthru FPGA image" or "Loading VC Interleaving FPGA image". More detail is in [firmware](firmware.md).

`/usr/lib/deckard-fpga/` also contains `cam_setup`, `cam_status`, `fpga_power_en.sh`, `fpga_power_disable.sh`, `pulse_room_led`, `read_reg`, `write_reg`, `reset_fpga` and `reset_cam_stats.sh`. None of these were run.

## Interpretation

*This section is interpretation, not observation. It combines the facts above with general knowledge and may be wrong.*

**A plausible camera architecture.**

- **Six cameras Linux can see, in three pairs.** Two passthrough cameras (`arcimx616`) and four tracking cameras: `slam_*` (`og01a1b`) and `upper_*` (`og0ve10`). The SoC's machine string ends in `4slam 2et`, which reads like "four SLAM cameras, two eye-tracking cameras": the four tracking cameras plus a pair the kernel doesn't see.
- **The FPGA as a camera aggregator.** The bitstreams are named `csi_agg`, and the other variant is "VC Interleaving". MIPI CSI-2 can carry several streams over one link using virtual channels (VCs), so the FPGA probably sits between some sensors and the SoC's camera inputs and merges their streams. The default, `passthru`, would forward them unchanged. Which cameras go through it isn't known. The `cam_setup` and `cam_status` tools beside the loader fit that.
- **XRService as the vision pipeline.** It holds `/dev/media0`, the tracking-camera sub-devices and capture nodes, and its strings name the camera ICP and EVA firmware ([firmware](firmware.md#camera-icp-and-evacvp)). It likely runs tracking and passthrough on the SoC's camera and vision blocks.
- **Eye tracking off the V4L2 path.** `dsp_service` has "ET Camera Streaming" and a cDSP "gazenet" thread ([firmware](firmware.md#adsp-and-cdsp)), and `eyetracking` runs with `-b CDSP`. The eye cameras are probably read and processed on the cDSP. OmniVision's OV6211 is a small sensor often used for eye tracking, and the aDSP's `[OV6211]` log tag ([above](#cameras)) names it, so the unbound `ov6211` and `ov6710` drivers ([kernel](kernel.md#other-frame-specific-drivers-in-the-tree)) may be left over from hardware that routed eye cameras through Linux. [OpenXR → eye tracking](openxr.md#eye-tracking-foveation-hands-and-passthrough) has the logged pipeline.

## EEPROM

**Tag: Internal.** `/usr/lib/deckard-eeprom/eeprom_console` (not on `PATH`) reads and writes the headset's EEPROM data. The tool groups it into four logical sections (`bootloader`, `core`, `vrcal`, `strap`), and the kernel exposes three EEPROM device nodes (listed below).

```sh
E=/usr/lib/deckard-eeprom/eeprom_console
$E help
$E get board_revision
$E print_all > ~/eeprom-backup.txt   # contains serials and MACs; keep it private
```

Readable items include `board_revision`, `board_minor`, `imu_rev`, `unit_config`, `ipd_min`, `ipd_max`, `prox_near`/`mid`/`far`, `prox_noise`, `diplexer`, `strap_revision`, `audio_module_vendor`, plus serial numbers for the unit, board, fan, heat pipes and audio modules, and the Wi-Fi/BLE MAC addresses.

The EEPROM also has `device_config`, `xrservice` and `eyetracking` items: compressed copies of the calibration files kept in `/persist`. `/usr/lib/deckard-hw-support/restore-calibration` uses them (`verify`, `backup [file]`, `restore-from-eeprom [--force]`).

**Don't run `reset`, `lock`, `unlock` or `upgrade` unless you have a backup.** Per `eeprom_console help`, they act on the `bootloader`, `core`, `vrcal` and `strap` sections.

The raw EEPROMs are on I²C at `/sys/bus/i2c/devices/{7-0050,7-0051,9-0050}/eeprom`. A udev rule (`99-eeprom.rules`) makes these mode 666, so any local user can read or write them. The matching nvmem nodes under `/sys/bus/nvmem/devices/` (`core_v2_eeprom5`, `strap_eeprom3`, `strap_v2_eeprom4`) stay root-only.

`vrconfig_serial` prints the unit serial (EEPROM first, then the SoC serial). Don't post its output publicly.

## Expansion port 5 V

`/sys/bus/platform/drivers/reg-valve_5v_exp/exp_vout_5v/control/enable` is chowned to `steamos` by udev (mode 644, so `steamos` can write it). The regulator's driver describes itself as "Valve 5V Expansion Regulator". `/persist` also has a file for it, `exp_5v_out_enable` (key `exp5v`; see [SteamVR → /persist](steamvr.md#per-device-config-in-persist)).

## Display

The panels are on DSI (`ae94000.dsi.0`). `displays_turn_off_drm_master` uses `modetest` to take DRM master and blank them, using a `4320x2160` mode on `DSI-1`. The `video` group can write the backlight brightness and `gamma_black_mode` on the DSI device. `/dev/dri/card0` and `renderD128` are mode 666. During a VR session `vrcompositor` is the DRM master; the connector, modes and DRM state are on [graphics → DRM/KMS](graphics.md#drmkms), and the backlight on [graphics → panel and backlight](graphics.md#panel-and-backlight).

---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/lostpanda85/frame-docs/blob/main/docs/controllers.md -->

# Controllers

The controllers' file and class names use **Roy** (`CRoyController`, `roy_*` configs, model numbers like `Roy_DV1_Left`). They don't appear to Linux as USB, Bluetooth or HID devices: no USB devices are enumerated, `bluetoothctl devices` lists none, and no `/dev/hidraw*` nodes exist.

This page is built from the files SteamVR ships in `/opt/steamvr/drivers/frame_controller/`, `/opt/steamvr/drivers/frame_hmd/` and `/opt/steamvr/drivers/cv/`, plus strings in `driver_cv.so`. No live controller data (battery levels, firmware versions, serials) is included.

**Tag: Internal**, except the input profile paths, which are **Public** (OpenVR input profile format).

## How they connect

What the files show:

- **A radio on SPI.** `disable_spi_hid.sh` (in `drivers/frame_hmd/resources/firmware/roy/`) prints `Removing spi_hid driver for dongle spi0.1 and binding spi driver`, then binds `spi0.1` to `spidev`. That's `/dev/spidev0.1`: `root:spidev`, mode 664, held open by `vrserver`, `vrcompositor`, `XRService` and `eyetracking`. In `driver_cv.so`, `CRoyDongle::InitializeSpi` and `CRoyDongle::SpiThreadFunc` handle the SPI side.
- **The radio's firmware.** `program_ble.sh`, in the same folder, runs `openocd` with `program roy_dongle_fw.hex preverify verify reset` over SWD (Arm's two-wire debug interface), using SoC GPIO pins (`gpiochip` for `f100000.pinctrl`, lines 51, 50 and 164). Whether it writes on a given boot wasn't determined ([firmware](firmware.md#headset-radio-nrf52)). Its recovery path runs openocd's `nrf52_recover`. `steamvr-program-ble.service` runs it at every boot ([services](services.md#hardware-and-power)). A second image, `roy_dongle_timesync_client_fw.hex`, sits in the same folder.
- **BLE.** The script is named `program_ble.sh`, the service is described as "SteamVR Controller BLE programmer", and `driver_cv.so` contains `CRoyController error: invald ble address` [sic]. (BLE is Bluetooth Low Energy.)
- **Time sync.** `driver_cv.so` log strings include `Controller %s timesync converged …` and `Dongle timestamp offset jump`.
- **Driver layout.** The `frame_controller` driver directory has `"resourceOnly": true` in its manifest: configs, input profiles, icons, render models and firmware. The controller code is in `drivers/cv/bin/linuxarm64/driver_cv.so`.

The chain those files describe, with the file behind each link where there is one:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    accTitle: Controller connection chain
    accDescr: The controllers reach the headset radio (nRF52) on spi0.1, called the dongle in code, over a radio link whose protocol is not covered. program_ble.sh, run at every boot, sends roy_dongle_fw.hex to the radio over SWD; whether it writes on a given boot was not determined. disable_spi_hid.sh binds spi0.1 to spidev, and the radio is exposed as /dev/spidev0.1, which vrserver, vrcompositor, XRService and eyetracking hold open. driver_cv.so (CRoyDongle) handles the SPI side.
    C["controllers"]
    PB["program_ble.sh<br/>run at every boot"]
    R["headset radio (nRF52)<br/>on spi0.1<br/>'dongle' in code"]
    DS["disable_spi_hid.sh"]
    S["/dev/spidev0.1"]
    CV["driver_cv.so"]
    P["vrserver, vrcompositor,<br/>XRService, eyetracking"]
    C -.->|"radio link;<br/>protocol not covered"| R
    PB -.->|"roy_dongle_fw.hex<br/>over SWD; write per<br/>boot not determined"| R
    R -->|"exposed as"| S
    DS -->|"binds spi0.1 to spidev"| S
    CV ---|"handles the SPI side<br/>(CRoyDongle)"| S
    S ---|"held open by"| P
```

Don't open `/dev/spidev0.1` yourself while SteamVR is running. Several processes are already sharing it.

## Tracking

Each controller's base config (`resources/config/frame_controller_{left,right}_base.json`) holds:

- `imu`: keys `plus_x`, `plus_z`, `position` (three numbers each)
- `lighthouse_config.modelPoints` / `modelNormals`: 18 entries each. What physical features they correspond to isn't stated in the files.
- `model_number`: `Steam_Frame_Controller_Left` / `_Right`, plus `manufacturer`, `revision` and `tracked_controller_role`

## Controls

From `resources/input/frame_controller_profile.json` (`controller_type: frame_controller`). The left controller has View and a D-pad; the right has Menu and A/B/X/Y. Every control reports touch as well as its main input. The skeleton inputs reference `/skeleton/hand/left` and `/skeleton/hand/right`.

| Input path | Left | Right | Type | Reports |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/input/system` | ✓ | ✓ | button | click, touch |
| `/input/view` | ✓ | | button | click, touch |
| `/input/menu` | | ✓ | button | click, touch |
| `/input/dpad_up` / `_down` / `_left` / `_right` | ✓ | | buttons | click, touch |
| `/input/a`, `/input/b`, `/input/x`, `/input/y` | | ✓ | buttons | click, touch |
| `/input/bumper` | ✓ | ✓ | button | click, touch |
| `/input/trigger` | ✓ | ✓ | trigger | value, click, touch |
| `/input/grip` | ✓ | ✓ | trigger | value, click, touch |
| `/input/thumbstick` | ✓ | ✓ | joystick | x/y, click, touch |
| `/input/thumbrest` | ✓ | ✓ | button | touch only; marked `InputValueVisibility_SteamVRInternal` in the profile |
| `/output/haptic` | ✓ | ✓ | vibration | |
| `/input/skeleton/left` / `right` | ✓ | ✓ | skeleton | finger poses |

Poses: `/pose/raw`, `/pose/base`, `/pose/handgrip`, `/pose/tip`, `/pose/gdc2015`, `/pose/openxr_grip` and `/pose/openxr_aim`.

**Mirroring.** The profile's `mirror_mappings` pair left and right controls: View ↔ Menu, and D-pad up/right/down/left ↔ Y/B/A/X.

### Touch and finger sensing

`driver_cv.so` contains more input paths than the public profile lists:

```
/input/capsense/{a,b,x,y,dpad,menu,system,bumper,trigger,grip,thumbstick,thumbrest,ring,pinky}
/input/finger/{index,middle,ring,pinky}
/input/grip/force
```

None of these paths are in `frame_controller_profile.json`.

### The headset's own buttons

`drivers/frame_hmd/resources/input/input_profile.json` (`controller_type: frame_hmd`) lists `/input/system`, `/input/volume_up` and `/input/volume_down`. The profile's only default binding is for `openvr.component.vrcompositor` (`vrcompositor_bindings_frame_hmd.json`).

## How existing games see them

`frame_controller_remapping.json` lists other controller types and how their input paths map onto the Frame controller's. Entries are listed by their `priority` value, highest first. When `simulate_render_model` is true, the app is given that controller's 3D model.

| App's controller type | Priority | `simulate_controller_type` / `simulate_render_model` |
|---|---|---|
| `khr_generic_controller` | 100 | false / false |
| `oculus_touch` | 95 | true / true |
| `pico_controller` | 93 | true / true |
| `knuckles` | 90 | true / true |
| `hand_interaction_ext` | 70 | false / false |
| `vive_controller` | 20 | true / true |
| `khr_simple_controller` | 10 | false / false |

Each entry lists `autoremappings` from the other controller's paths to Frame paths. For `khr_generic_controller`, for example, `/input/primary` maps to A on the right and D-pad down on the left, and `/input/secondary` maps to B on the right and D-pad left and right on the left controller.

`default_bindings` in the profile name these per-app binding files: `half_life_alyx_bindings_frame_controller.json` (plus `_left_` and `_single_` variants), `beat_saber_…`, `arizona_sunshine_vr_remake_…`, `batman_arkham_…`, `chromalab_…`, `accountingplus_…`, `doomvfr_…`, `in_death_legacy_…`, `pixelripped1989_…` and `pixelripped1995_…`. Others cover `steam.client` (`steam_vrgamepad_bindings_frame_controller.json`), `openvr.component.vrcompositor` and `vrlink.client`.

## Pairing and firmware updates

Both go through SteamVR [mailboxes](steamvr.md#mailboxes). The names below come from strings in `driver_cv.so` and from the shipped web UI's JavaScript. Strings show which names exist, not how they fit together, and none of these messages were sent.

### `frame_controller_pairing`

The mailbox name and these message types appear in `driver_cv.so`. The web UI doesn't reference this mailbox.

| Message `type` | Notes |
|---|---|
| `start_pairing`, `stop_pairing` | |
| `update_pairing_state` | Name only. Other field names in `driver_cv.so`: `is_pairing`, `paired_controllers`, `connected_controllers`, `expected_controllers`, `num_controller_slots`. |
| `identify_controller` | Payload unknown. The driver logs `CRoyPairing identify controller '%s' %s`. |
| `disconnect_controller`, `disconnect_all_controllers` | |
| `unpair_controller`, `unpair_all_controllers`, `unpair_disconnected_controllers` | |

Log strings in `driver_cv.so` that mention OOBE: `discovered new %s OOBE controller`, `attempting to connect to Left/Right OOBE controller candidate`, `new bootstrap` and `pairing to OOBE controller`.

### `lighthouse_pairing`

The web UI's pairing code sends `discover_dongles` and `start_pairing` (`{serial, timeoutSeconds: 10, sendStatusUpdates: true}`) to a mailbox called `lighthouse_pairing`. Neither `driver_cv.so` nor `vrserver` contains that name.

### `frame_controller_firmware_update`

This one appears both in `driver_cv.so` and in the web UI, which sends `{type: "update_state"}` and `start_update`.

| Message `type` | Notes |
|---|---|
| `update_state` | Name only. Other field names in `driver_cv.so`: `firmware_update_state`, `readytoupdate`. |
| `start_update` | Takes `{serial_number}` (not `serial`, as in pairing) |
| `identify_controller` | |

`resources/firmware/manifest.vrfirmware` maps hardware IDs to firmware images:

| Hardware ID | Name | Image |
|---|---|---|
| `0x1006010000000000` | Steam Frame DV1 Controller | `Alias`: `0x1006020000000000` |
| `0x1006020000000000` | Steam Frame DV2 Controller | `roy_controller_fw_uc_<version>.bin` |
| `0x1008010000000000` | Steam Frame PV Controller | `Alias`: `0x100a010000000000` |
| `0x100a010000000000`, `0x100a020000000000` | Steam Frame Controller | `roy_controller_fw_c_<version>.bin` |

The `0x1006020000000000` entry uses the `VRCUCBin` key and the `_uc` image; the `0x100a010000000000` entry uses `VRCBin` and the `_c` image. If a controller's firmware is older than the driver's minimum, SteamVR logs `firmware does not meet minimum required version` and `driver_cv.so` also contains `Compositor requires mandatory firmware update (402)`.

## Hardware revisions

`resources/config/` has base configs for these revisions:

| Config | Model number | Model points |
|---|---|---|
| `roy_pocf_*` | `Roy_K2V3_*_CV` | 17 |
| `roy_ev1_*` | `Roy_EV1_*_CV` | 18 |
| `roy_ev1_5_*` | `Roy_EV1.5_*_CV` | 18 |
| `roy_ev2_*` | `Roy_EV2_*` | 18 |
| `roy_ev2_ergo_*` | `Roy_EV2_Playtest_Ergo_*_CV` | 18 |
| `roy_dv1_*` | `Roy_DV1_*` | 18 |
| `frame_controller_dv2_*` | `Steam_Frame_Controller_*` | 18 |
| `frame_controller_*` | `Steam_Frame_Controller_*` | 18 |

## Using the controllers from your own code

- **OpenVR apps**: bind to the `frame_controller` paths above, or to one of the controller types in the remapping table.
- **OpenXR apps**: the runtime is registered at `~/.config/openxr/1/active_runtime.json`. SteamVR has Frame-specific profiles, `/interaction_profiles/valve/frame_controller` and `…/frame_controller_valve` (extension `XR_VALVE_frame_controller_interaction`), and apps' stored bindings for `frame_controller` record `frame_controller_valve` ([OpenXR → interaction profiles](openxr.md#interaction-profiles)). Which profile `xrGetCurrentInteractionProfile` reports for the controller still wasn't determined; the remapping table lists the profiles SteamVR maps from.
- **Inspecting live state**: `vrcmd --dumpsensors` lists tracked devices with their sensor positions, and its device lines include serial numbers, so redact them before sharing. `--pollcontrollers` and `--prop` are also in `vrcmd --help`, but weren't run.
- **The SteamVR web console** is served at `http://127.0.0.1:27062/console/index.html` on the headset.

## Not covered

- The radio protocol between the controllers and the headset
- Controller battery reporting and charging (`driver_cv.so` contains a `battery_capacity` string; no live readings were taken)
- What `roy_dongle_timesync_client_fw.hex` is used for
- Steam Input's own configuration for these controllers inside the Steam client

# Power, suspend and thermals

This page covers how the headset sleeps and wakes, who gets a say before it does, what the power button does, how the kernel handles heat, and how CPU and GPU clocks are governed. Battery and charging state, power rails, the fan and the status LED are on [hardware](hardware.md); this page links there instead of repeating them.

Everything here comes from sysfs and procfs reads, config files, `systemd-inhibit --list`, logind's D-Bus properties, `strings` on binaries and the journal on the headset surveyed. The headset wasn't suspended, and no power setting was changed.

## What matters

- **Suspend is deep.** `/sys/power/mem_sleep` selects `deep`, and every suspend in the journal logged `PM: suspend entry (deep)`. ([Sleep states](#sleep-states))
- **The kernel has no hibernation, but logind lists it.** `CONFIG_HIBERNATION` isn't set and `/sys/power/disk` doesn't exist, yet logind's `SleepOperation` includes `hibernate` and `suspend-then-hibernate`. ([Sleep states](#sleep-states))
- **The power key goes to Steam, not logind.** logind has `HandlePowerKey=ignore`, and `steamos-powerbuttond` sends presses to the Steam client as `steam://shortpowerpress`. ([logind](#logind-and-sleep-configuration), [Power button](#power-button))
- **Seven processes hold sleep inhibitors, all `delay`, none `block`.** ([Sleep inhibitors](#sleep-inhibitors))
- **The only in-kernel throttling is GPU devfreq at 95 °C.** CPU thermal zones have only a 110 °C critical trip, and the fan is driven from userspace. ([Thermal zones](#thermal-zones))
- **The CPU governor is `schedutil`, set at login; the GPU runs 231–903 MHz under `simple_ondemand`.** ([CPU and GPU frequency](#cpu-and-gpu-frequency))

## Sleep states

**Tag: Public (upstream).**

| Source | Value |
|---|---|
| `/sys/power/state` | `freeze mem` |
| `/sys/power/mem_sleep` | `s2idle [deep]` (deep is selected) |
| `/sys/power/disk` | doesn't exist |
| `/proc/config.gz` | `CONFIG_SUSPEND=y`, `CONFIG_PM_SLEEP=y`, `CONFIG_PM_WAKELOCKS=y`, `# CONFIG_HIBERNATION is not set` |
| `/sys/power/pm_async`, `sync_on_suspend`, `freeze_filesystems` | `1`, `1`, `0` |
| `/sys/power/pm_freeze_timeout` | `20000` |
| `/sys/power/wake_lock` | empty |

The journal's suspend cycles all logged `Performing sleep operation 'suspend'...` followed by `PM: suspend entry (deep)`. The kernel has no hibernation support, yet logind's `SleepOperation` property lists `suspend-then-hibernate`, `suspend` and `hibernate`, and `hibernate-prepare.service` ("Prepare Temporary Hibernation Swap", `WantedBy=hibernate.target`) runs `hibernate-swap-helper.sh create` ([services](services.md#boot-updates-and-filesystem)). Swap is `/dev/zram0` plus the 1 GB `/home/swapfile` (`/proc/swaps`).

Devices whose `power/wakeup` is `enabled`:

| Device (under `/sys/devices/platform/soc@0/`) | What it is |
|---|---|
| `c400000.spmi:pmic@0:pon@1300:pwrkey` | Power key |
| `c400000.spmi:pmic@0:rtc@6100` and its `alarmtimer` | PMIC real-time clock |
| `c400000.spmi:pmic@7:charger@2600/power_supply/pm8550b-charger` | Charger |
| `c400000.spmi:pmic@7:typec@2b00/power_supply/tcpm-source-psy-…` | USB-C port |
| `ac0000.geniqup/a88000.i2c/i2c-7/7-0036/power_supply/max1720x_bat_7-36` | Battery fuel gauge |
| `1c00000.pcie/…/0000:01:00.0/mhi0` | The Wi-Fi chip's MHI bus ([Wi-Fi](wireless.md#wi-fi-chip-and-driver)) |
| `c228000`, `c229000`, `c22a000` `.thermal-sensor` | SoC temperature sensors |

### CPU idle

`/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpuidle/current_driver` is `psci_idle` and the governor is `menu`. Each CPU has two states, `WFI` (latency 1 µs) and a power-collapse state:

| CPUs | Second state | Description | Latency |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–4 | `cpu-sleep-0-0` | `silver-rail-power-collapse` | 1300 µs |
| 5, 6 | `cpu-sleep-1-0` | `gold-rail-power-collapse` | 1900 µs |
| 7 | `cpu-sleep-2-0` | `gold-plus-rail-power-collapse` | 1850 µs |

## logind and sleep configuration

**Tag: Public (upstream)** for logind; **Internal** for the drop-in.

`systemd-analyze cat-config systemd/logind.conf` shows one active setting, from `/etc/systemd/logind.conf.d/10-logind-no-powerbutton.conf` (owned by `deckard-hw-support`):

```ini
# Tell `systemd` not to bother with the powerbutton, `powerbuttond` will handle it.
[Login]
HandlePowerKey=ignore
```

`systemd-analyze cat-config systemd/sleep.conf` shows only `/etc/systemd/sleep.conf` (owned by `systemd`), with every setting commented out. logind's properties on the system bus:

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| `HandlePowerKey` | `ignore` |
| `HandleSuspendKey` | `suspend` |
| `HandleLidSwitch` | `suspend` |
| `IdleAction` | `ignore` |
| `IdleActionUSec` | 1800000000 (30 min) |

logind logs `Watching system buttons on /dev/input/event0 (pmic_pwrkey)` and `Power key pressed short.`

## Power button

**Tag: Internal.** `steamos-powerbuttond.service` is a user unit ("Power Button daemon for SteamOS") from the `steamos-powerbuttond` package (3.2+git4403691c-5). It runs `/usr/lib/hwsupport/steamos-powerbuttond`, an aarch64 ELF ([services](services.md#vr-session-user-units)). The unit has:

- `Requisite=steamvr.service`
- `ExecCondition=/bin/bash -c '[[ $(vrdevice_path model) != EV1 ]]'`, under the comment "Do NOT run powerbuttond on an EV1, because it only has a single button, and we don't want it to " (the comment ends there)

How it finds the button:

- The package's hwdb file, `/usr/lib/udev/hwdb.d/70-steamos-power-button.hwdb`, has an entry under the comment `#deckard` matching `evdev:name:pmic_pwrkey:*`. Most other entries match DMI vendors of PC handhelds.
- `udevadm info /dev/input/event0` shows `STEAMOS_POWER_BUTTON=1` and tags `power-switch`, `uaccess` and `seat`. The rule `70-steamos-power-button.rules` gives such devices `MODE="0660"` and `TAG+="uaccess"`.
- The daemon logs `Found power button device at /dev/input/event0`; `/sys/class/input/event0/device/name` is `pmic_pwrkey`.

The binary's strings include `libevdev`, `short`, `long`, `steam://%spowerpress`, `%s/.steam/steam/steamrtarm64/steam`, `submitting %s power press to steam`, `skipping power button push since we are already suspending or still actively resuming`, and `org.freedesktop.login1.Manager`.

One short press, as the journal recorded it:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    accTitle: A short power-button press leading to suspend
    accDescr: The pmic_pwrkey input device reports a key press. logind logs "Power key pressed short." and does nothing because HandlePowerKey is ignore. steamos-powerbuttond reads the same event, logs "submitting short power press to steam", and runs the Steam binary with a steam://shortpowerpress URL, which is forwarded to the running Steam client. How Steam then asks for suspend was not determined. logind logs "The system will suspend now!", signals the delay inhibitors, the system-sleep hooks run with pre, and the kernel logs "PM: suspend entry (deep)".
    participant K as pmic_pwrkey<br/>(/dev/input/event0)
    participant L as systemd-logind
    participant P as steamos-powerbuttond
    participant S as Steam client
    participant I as delay inhibitors
    K->>L: key event
    Note over L: "Power key pressed short."<br/>HandlePowerKey=ignore
    K->>P: key event (libevdev)
    P->>S: steam://shortpowerpress<br/>("command line was forwarded")
    S-->>L: suspend request (how: not determined)
    Note over L: "The system will suspend now!"
    L->>I: sleep notification
    Note over L: system-sleep hooks (pre),<br/>then "PM: suspend entry (deep)"
```

A press during resume logged `skipping power button push since we are already suspending or still actively resuming`. What a long press does on the Steam side wasn't observed.

## Sleep inhibitors

**Tag: Public (upstream)** for the inhibitor mechanism; **Internal** for most of the holders. `systemd-inhibit --list` in a normal VR session (all `delay`, none `block`):

| Who | Process | What | Why (as registered) |
|---|---|---|---|
| NetworkManager | `NetworkManager` (root) | sleep | "NetworkManager needs to turn off networks" |
| Realtime Kit | `rtkit-daemon` (root) | sleep | "Demote realtime scheduling and stop canary." |
| UPower | `upowerd` (root) | sleep | "Pause device polling" |
| dsp_service | `dsp_service` (root) | sleep | "dsp_service needs to clean DSP hardware interfaces" |
| led-control | `ledcontrol` (root) | shutdown:sleep | "Set status LED before sleep" |
| XRService | `XRService` (`steamos`) | sleep | "XRService needs to clean hardware interfaces" |
| vrserver | `vrserver` (`steamos`) | sleep | "Driver standby" |

`vrserver`'s strings include `PrepareForSleep`, `[CSystemSleepNotifier] Failed to match PrepareForSleep.`, `Failed to acquire %s inhibitor: %s`, `Steam reports host suspend imminent; fading to %.0f%% over %.1fs, then to black over %.1fs` and `Steam reports host suspend cancelled; fading in over %.1fs`. `dsp_service`'s suspend handling (shutting the DSPs down, re-binding the USB-C port driver after resume) is on [Firmware → Suspend and resume](firmware.md#suspend-and-resume). `ledcontrol` logs `led-control received process_logind_sleep_event (suspend)` and `(resume)` ([Hardware access → Status LED](hardware.md#status-led)).

## System-sleep hooks

**Tag: Internal.** `/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/` holds five files; `/etc/systemd/system-sleep/` doesn't exist. Two of the scripts say they are "designed to be invoked by systemd-sleep" with `<pre|post>` and the sleep mode as arguments.

| File | Package | Mode | What it does (from its contents) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `00-ledcontrol.sh` | `deckard-led-control` | `0644` (not executable) | Creates `/run/deckardcharger`, empties `power_event`, then writes `suspend` there on `pre` and `resume` on `post` |
| `50-softapcmd-refresh-on-resume.sh` | `softapmanager` | `0755` | On `post`, logs "System resume: refreshing softap" and runs `softapcmd delayrefresh` ([local IPC](local-ipc.md#control-socket)) |
| `ath12k-irq-respread.sh` | `steamos-customizations-deckard` | `0755` | On `pre`, saves the effective CPU of every IRQ whose `/proc/interrupts` name matches `ITS-PCI-MSI` to `/run/irq-respread.state`. On `post`, writes each saved CPU back to `/proc/irq/<n>/smp_affinity_list` if it changed. |
| `hibernate-post.sh` | `steamos-customizations-deckard` | `0755` | Only after `hibernate`: runs `hibernate-swap-helper.sh cleanup` and `steamos-bootconf --set boot-attempts 0` |
| `modules-reload.sh` | `steamos-customizations-deckard` | `0755` | Only if `/home/deck/.force-ath11k-reload` exists: unloads `ath11k-pci` on `pre` and reloads it on `post` |

The comment at the top of `ath12k-irq-respread.sh` gives its reason: "Deep suspend hot-unplugs CPUs 1-7, so every IRQ migrates to CPU0 … On resume only *managed* IRQs are moved back … Non-managed MSIs such as ath12k's 16 vectors stay on CPU0 until reboot, and so does all of their NET_RX work." The journal on the headset surveyed has `irq-respread: saved … IRQs matching 'ITS-PCI-MSI'` and `irq-respread: moved … IRQs, 0 failed` lines, and `System resume: refreshing softap`, once per resume. No `00-ledcontrol.sh` output is logged, since the script doesn't print anything.

Other units tied to suspend: `deckard-fpga.service` has `Conflicts=suspend.target`, and `deckard-fpga-resume.service` restarts it afterwards ([Firmware → FPGA bitstreams](firmware.md#fpga-bitstreams)).

## Thermal zones

**Tag: Public (upstream).** Values are from `/sys/class/thermal/`. There are 48 thermal zones. All use the `step_wise` policy and are `enabled` (`available_policies`: `power_allocator user_space step_wise`; `CONFIG_THERMAL_DEFAULT_GOV_STEP_WISE=y`). Trip points, in °C:

| Zones | passive | hot | critical |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cpu0`, `cpu1`, and `cpu2`–`cpu7` `-top`/`-bottom` (plus `cpu7-middle`) `-thermal` | | | 110 |
| `aoss0`–`2`, `cpuss0`–`3`, `video`, `ddr`, `camera0`/`1`, `nsphvx0`/`1`, `nsphmx0`–`3`, `modem3` `-thermal` | | 110 | 115 |
| `gpuss-0`–`4-thermal` | 95 | 110 | 115 |
| PMIC zones: `pm8010-m`/`-n`, `pm8550`, `pm8550b`, `pm8550vs-c`/`d`/`e`/`g`, `pm8550ve` `-thermal` | 95 | 115 | |
| `max1720x_bat_7-36` (battery) | | | (no trip points) |

Cooling devices:

| Device | Type | `max_state` | Bound to a zone? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cooling_device0`–`3` | `cpufreq-cpu0`, `-cpu2`, `-cpu5`, `-cpu7` | 17, 31, 28, 31 | No |
| `cooling_device4` | `devfreq-3d00000.gpu` | 11 | Yes: each `gpuss-*` zone's trip 0 (passive, 95 °C) |
| `cooling_device5` | `ath12k_thermal` | 100 | No |

So the only in-kernel throttling binding is GPU devfreq on the GPU zones. CPU zones have only a critical trip. The fan is driven from userspace by `deckard-fan-control`, whose config's first device entry is `cpu7_middle_thermal` ([Hardware access → Thermals and the fan](hardware.md#thermals-and-the-fan)).

## CPU and GPU frequency

**Tag: Public (upstream)** for the interfaces; **Internal** for the values SteamOS sets. The governor and frequency caps are also exposed through SteamOS Manager's `CpuScaling1`, `GpuPerformanceLevel1` and `PerformanceProfile1` interfaces ([D-Bus APIs → `PerformanceProfile1`](dbus.md#performanceprofile1)).

| cpufreq policy | CPUs | Driver | Governor | Hardware range |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `policy0` | 0–1 | `qcom-cpufreq-hw` | `schedutil` | 364.8 MHz – 2.2656 GHz |
| `policy2` | 2–4 | `qcom-cpufreq-hw` | `schedutil` | 499.2 MHz – 3.1488 GHz |
| `policy5` | 5–6 | `qcom-cpufreq-hw` | `schedutil` | 499.2 MHz – 2.9568 GHz |
| `policy7` | 7 | `qcom-cpufreq-hw` | `schedutil` | 480 MHz – 3.0528 GHz |

- The kernel's default governor is `performance` (`CONFIG_CPU_FREQ_DEFAULT_GOV_PERFORMANCE=y`). At login, the user unit `steamos-scheduler.service` applies `GOVERNOR=schedutil` and `SCHEDULER=lavd` from `/etc/default/steamos-scheduler` ([services](services.md#vr-session-user-units)).
- `/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/boost` is `0`.
- GPU: `/sys/devices/platform/soc@0/3d00000.gpu/devfreq/3d00000.gpu` uses `simple_ondemand` (available: `userspace performance simple_ondemand`), 231–903 MHz in 12 steps. The UFS controller (`1d84000.ufshc`) is the only other devfreq device, also `simple_ondemand`.
- SteamOS Manager logged `Can't add GpuPowerProfile1 interface: No GPU power profile driver configured` at session start.

## Battery and low-battery handling

**Tag: Public (upstream).** Charge state, the charger daemon's `/run/deckardcharger/` files and the fuel gauge are on [Hardware access → Battery and charging](hardware.md#battery-and-charging) and [Firmware → Battery fuel-gauge settings](firmware.md#battery-fuel-gauge-settings).

UPower 1.91.1 runs with `/etc/UPower/UPower.conf` (owned by `upower`; `UPower.conf.d/` holds only a README): `UsePercentageForPolicy=true`, `PercentageLow=20.0`, `PercentageCritical=5.0`, `PercentageAction=2.0`, `CriticalPowerAction=HybridSleep`. The power supplies it can see are `max1720x_bat_7-36`, `pm8550b-charger` and the USB-C port's `tcpm-source-psy-…`.

## Proximity sensor

**Tag: Internal.** The sensor is a VCNL4040 on IIO `iio:device2` ([Hardware access → Other sensors](hardware.md#other-sensors)). What reads it, as far as files and strings show:

- **SteamVR's CV driver.** `driver_cv.so` contains `vrdevice_path prox_sensor`, `/usr/lib/deckard-eeprom/eeprom_console get prox_far`, ` [CHmdDirectDeviceControl] Proximity sensing enable: proxfar %d `, ` [CHmdDirectDeviceControl] Proximity sensing disabled (cannot read proxfar)`, `Device JSON: Overriding proximityEnable to %d (%s)` and the input path `/proximity`. `vrserver` contains `UpdateProximitySensorStates`, `k_EButton_ProximitySensor` and `Prop_ContainsProximitySensor_Bool`.
- **`proxmicmute`.** An OpenVR client that sets the capture volume of `VA_DEC0` and `VA_DEC1` on `hw:0`. It contains no IIO path ([Audio → Proximity-based mic mute](audio.md#proximity-based-mic-mute)).
- **`prox_sensor_val`**, a shell script that `cat`s the first `in_proximity_raw` under `/sys/bus/iio/devices/`.

`driver_cv.so` also has standby strings (`[CCVTrackedHmdDriver] in StateStandby`, `Device %s powering off upon entering standby.`). Whether taking the headset off leads to standby, display-off or suspend wasn't observed.

## Interpretation

*This section is interpretation, not observation. It combines the facts above with general knowledge and may be wrong.*

- **Steam is the power policy.** logind is told to ignore the power key and idle, and the button daemon forwards presses to Steam as a URL. With `HandlePowerKey=ignore`, logind would take no action on the press it logs, and with `IdleAction=ignore` the 30-minute `IdleActionUSec` would go unused. Steam decides whether a press means suspend, a menu or a power-off. The same daemon and hwdb file serve the PC handhelds listed in it, so the Frame likely shares the Steam Deck-style flow.
- **Thermal management is mostly in userspace.** With CPU cooling devices unbound, CPU temperature is held by the fan daemon and by the frequency caps in SteamOS Manager's performance profiles. The kernel only steps in for the GPU at 95 °C and at critical trips.
- **`00-ledcontrol.sh` may be dead.** systemd-sleep generally runs only executable hooks. `ledcontrol` also holds its own logind inhibitor and gets suspend and resume events directly, so the LED may not need the hook at all.
- **`proxmicmute` gets proximity through SteamVR.** It's an OpenVR client with no IIO path, so its proximity information would come from SteamVR's events rather than from the sensor directly.
- **Hibernate leftovers.** The hibernate helper, `hibernate-post.sh` and `modules-reload.sh` (which names `ath11k-pci` and `/home/deck`) look like Steam Deck pieces carried over in `steamos-customizations-deckard`.

## How to inspect this yourself

All read-only. Don't use `systemctl suspend`, `echo mem > /sys/power/state`, `fanspeed -s` or `steamosctl set-*` to explore.

```sh
cat /sys/power/state /sys/power/mem_sleep
ls -l /usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/
systemd-analyze cat-config systemd/logind.conf systemd/sleep.conf
systemd-inhibit --list
busctl get-property org.freedesktop.login1 /org/freedesktop/login1 \
  org.freedesktop.login1.Manager HandlePowerKey IdleAction SleepOperation
journalctl -g 'PM: suspend|irq-respread|refreshing softap'   # all boots; add -b for this one
journalctl --user -b -u steamos-powerbuttond

# Thermal zones, trip points and which cooling device each zone uses
cd /sys/class/thermal
for z in thermal_zone*; do
  printf '%s:' "$(cat $z/type)"
  for t in $z/trip_point_*_type; do printf ' %s=%s' "$(cat $t)" "$(cat ${t%_type}_temp)"; done
  echo
done
for c in cooling_device*; do echo "$c $(cat $c/type) max=$(cat $c/max_state)"; done

# CPU and GPU governors
grep . /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/policy*/scaling_governor
cat /sys/devices/platform/soc@0/3d00000.gpu/devfreq/3d00000.gpu/governor
```

## Not determined

- How Steam asks for suspend after a power-button press (a logind call, SteamOS Manager, or something else)
- What a long press does
- What `CriticalPowerAction=HybridSleep` does on a kernel without hibernation, and whether `deckard_charge_daemon`'s `secs_until_shutdown_request` ([hardware](hardware.md#rundeckardcharger)) or UPower acts first
- Whether `00-ledcontrol.sh` runs (it isn't executable)
- Whether removing the headset leads to standby, display-off or suspend, and after how long
- Why the `cpufreq` cooling devices aren't bound to any thermal zone, and what throttles the CPUs before 110 °C, if anything
- What the `ath12k_thermal` cooling device is used for

# Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and streaming

The headset has one WCN7850 chip, which `lspci` and the `ath12k` module description name as Qualcomm Technologies: Wi-Fi on PCIe, driven by `ath12k`, and Bluetooth on a UART. The Wi-Fi side runs two networks at once: a normal client connection on `wlan0`, managed by NetworkManager and `wpa_supplicant`, and the headset's own access point on `wlanap`, run by `softapmanager`. `vrlink` (in `/opt/steamvr/tools/vrlink`) contains strings for a UDP link to a PC and a V4L2 decoder found through `vrdevice_path video_decode`; it wasn't run.

Everything here comes from `iw phy`, `iw dev`, `iw reg get`, `nmcli`, `bluetoothctl show`, `lspci`, `modinfo`, sysfs, config files, `v4l2-ctl` format queries and `strings` on binaries. No scan, connection, pairing or radio change was made. MAC addresses, network names, the regulatory country and paired devices are left out on purpose.

## What matters

- **One WCN7850 handles Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.** Wi-Fi is on PCIe, driven by `ath12k`; Bluetooth is on a UART, driven by `hci_uart_qca`. The controllers don't use this Bluetooth controller; they use a separate nRF52 radio. ([Wi-Fi chip and driver](#wi-fi-chip-and-driver), [Bluetooth controller](#bluetooth-controller))
- **Client and access point run at once.** `wlan0` (client, NetworkManager) and `wlanap` (access point, `softapmanager`) were both up on `phy0`. ([Interfaces](#interfaces), [The headset's own access point](#the-headsets-own-access-point))
- **RX reorder timeout is 2 ms on every queue, and Wi-Fi power save is off.** `ath12k.conf` sets the RX reorder timeout to 2 ms on all four queues, and NetworkManager drop-ins turn Wi-Fi power save off; `iw` reported `Power save: off` on both interfaces. ([Wi-Fi chip and driver](#wi-fi-chip-and-driver), [NetworkManager and wpa_supplicant](#networkmanager-and-wpa_supplicant))
- **The radio is 2×2, and 320 MHz is advertised only for AP and mesh on 6 GHz.** `iw phy` shows `TX 0x3 RX 0x3` antennas and two spatial streams; `managed` mode on 6 GHz goes up to 160 MHz. ([What the radio supports](#what-the-radio-supports-iw-phy))
- **PC streaming is known only from `vrlink`'s strings.** They show a UDP link to a PC and a V4L2 decoder found through `vrdevice_path video_decode`. `vrlink` wasn't running, and no streaming session was observed. ([PC streaming](#pc-streaming-vrlink))

## Wi-Fi chip and driver

**Tag: Public (upstream)** for the driver; **Internal** for Valve's module options.

| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Chip | WCN7850 (`Wi-Fi 7 Hardware name: wcn7850 hw2.0`) | kernel log ([firmware](firmware.md#wi-fi-and-bluetooth)) |
| PCI name | `Qualcomm Technologies, Inc WCN785x Wi-Fi 7(802.11be) 320MHz 2x2 [FastConnect 7800] (rev 01)` | `lspci -s 01:00.0` |
| Bus | PCIe `0000:01:00.0`, `PCI_ID=17CB:1107`, with an `mhi0` child | sysfs |
| Driver | `ath12k_wifi7_pci`; modules `ath12k` ("Driver support for Qualcomm Technologies WLAN devices") and `ath12k_wifi7` ("Driver support for Qualcomm Technologies 802.11be WLAN devices") | `/sys/class/net/wlan0/device/uevent`, `lsmod`, `modinfo` |
| Firmware | `ath12k/WCN7850/hw2.0/`, board file `board_77.bin` | [Firmware → Wi-Fi (`ath12k`)](firmware.md#wi-fi-ath12k) |
| `rfkill` | `rfkill1`, type `wlan`, `phy0`, soft and hard unblocked | `/sys/class/rfkill/` |

`modinfo -p ath12k` lists these parameters (descriptions quoted exactly, including the type in parentheses):

| Parameter | Description (from `modinfo -p`) | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `rx_reorder_timeout` | `RX reorder timeout in ms. Use one value for all ACs or four values BE,BK,VI,VO (0 means use driver defaults) Example: set all to 2: rx_reorder_timeout=2 set only VO to 2: rx_reorder_timeout=0,0,0,2 (array of uint)` | `2,2,2,2` |
| `egap` | `<enable>[,<flags>[,<inactivity_ms>[,<wait_ms>]]]: empty fields default (0,0x4,1000,1000). flags: 0x1=PHY error detection, 0x2=by station PS state, 0x4=by inactivity; ms times 1 to 300000 (string)` | `0,0x4,1000,1000` |
| `gtx` | `Green TX, applied as each vdev comes up: -1=BDF default (default), 0=disable, 1=enable (int)` | `-1` |
| `default_bdf` | `Name of BDF file to load if board_id is not set (string)` | empty |
| `mac_addr` | `Override the internal MAC address (format aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff) (string)` | empty |
| `ftm_mode` | `Boots up in factory test mode (bool)` | `N` |
| `debug_mask` | `Debugging mask (uint)` | `0` |

`rx_reorder_timeout` comes from `/usr/lib/modprobe.d/ath12k.conf` (owned by `deckard-hw-support`). Its comments explain the history. The first plan was to shorten only the VI (video) queue, "to reduce reorder timeout when transmitting from the dongle -> HMD, where we have restricted retries severely in order to prioritize low-latency video streams. We will tag the vrlink packets as VI (video) when coming out of the dongle." The active line sets all four queues instead: "DISREGARD ALL OF THAT. Instead just set everything to 2ms. We want to avoid head-of-line blocking for all traffic on all interfaces."

The Wi-Fi chip's MHI device is a wakeup source ([power](power.md#sleep-states)), and a sleep hook re-spreads the chip's 16 MSI interrupts after resume ([Power, suspend and thermals → System-sleep hooks](power.md#system-sleep-hooks)). A board temperature channel named `…_at_wifi_input` is on [Hardware access → Thermals and the fan](hardware.md#thermals-and-the-fan).

## What the radio supports (`iw phy`)

**Tag: Public (upstream).** One wiphy, `phy0`.

| Band | Standards and widths | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Band 1 (2.4 GHz) | HT20/HT40; HE with `HE40/2.4GHz`; EHT MCS map for ≤ 80 MHz | |
| Band 2 (5 GHz) | VHT up to 160 MHz; HE40/HE80 and HE160; EHT maps for ≤ 80 and 160 MHz | Some channels marked "radar detection" |
| Band 4 (6 GHz) | HE40/HE80 and HE160; EHT up to 160 MHz for `managed`, and "320MHz in 6GHz Supported" with a 320 MHz MCS map for `AP` and `mesh point` | |

- **Streams:** `Available Antennas: TX 0x3 RX 0x3`. HE: 1 or 2 streams at MCS 0–11. EHT maps (`0x222222`): max NSS 2 for MCS 0–9, 10–11 and 12–13.
- **Interface modes:** `managed`, `AP`, `monitor`, `P2P-client`, `P2P-GO`, `P2P-device`.
- **Valid combination:** `#{ managed } <= 1, #{ AP, P2P-client, P2P-GO } <= 16, #{ P2P-device } <= 1, total <= 16, #channels <= 2, STA/AP BI must match`.
- **Ciphers:** TKIP, CCMP-128/256, GCMP-128/256, CMAC/CMAC-256, GMAC-128/256.
- **WoWLAN:** wake on disconnect, magic packet, pattern match (up to 22 patterns), GTK rekey failure, network detection (up to 16 match sets); can do GTK rekeying.
- **Extended features include:** `BEACON_PROTECTION`, `BSS_COLOR`, `PUNCT` (preamble puncturing in AP mode), `FILS_STA`, `FILS_DISCOVERY`, `UNSOL_BCAST_PROBE_RESP`, `STA_TX_PWR`, `TXQS`, `POWERED_ADDR_CHANGE`, `CONTROL_PORT_OVER_NL80211`.
- **Commands include** `start_ap`, `channel_switch`, `start_p2p_device`, `remain_on_channel` and `assoc_mlo_reconf`.

`iw dev` showed `txpower 18.00 dBm` on both `wlan0` and `wlanap`, and `iw dev <if> get power_save` returned `Power save: off` on both.

## Regulatory handling

**Tag: Public (upstream)** for the mechanism; **Internal** for Steam's use of it.

- `wireless-regdb` 2026.02.04-3 ships `regulatory.db` and `regulatory.db.p7s`; the initramfs includes both ([Firmware → The firmware loader](firmware.md#the-firmware-loader)).
- `/sys/module/cfg80211/parameters/ieee80211_regdom` holds a two-letter country code. `/usr/lib/modprobe.d/` sets no `cfg80211` options. Where the value comes from wasn't determined.
- `iw reg get` prints the global domain and a separate block for `phy#0 (self-managed)`, with its own rule list. That list uses the flags `DFS`, `NO-OUTDOOR`, `PASSIVE-SCAN`, `AUTO-BW` and per-range `NO-80MHZ`/`NO-160MHZ`/`NO-320MHZ`. The rules themselves aren't reproduced here because they identify the country.
- `cfg80211` also has `cfg80211_block_scans` (value `0`), `cfg80211_disable_40mhz_24ghz` (`N`) and `bss_entries_limit` (`1000`). `softapmanager` contains the path of the first one ([Local sockets and IPC → Streaming socket](local-ipc.md#streaming-socket)).
- `steamclient.so` contains `CRemoteClientSoftAP::OnIPCountry` and the soft-AP command `set-fallback-country-code\t%s`. The soft AP's `get-channels` reply is grouped by what's usable in the current regulatory country ([Local sockets and IPC → Control socket](local-ipc.md#control-socket)).

## Interfaces

| Interface | Type (`iw dev`) | Managed by | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wlan0` | `managed` | NetworkManager + `wpa_supplicant` | Client connection; firewall zone `public` ([network services](network-services.md#port-map)) |
| `wlanap` | `AP` | `softapmanager` (`hostapd`, `dnsmasq`) | NetworkManager lists it as `unmanaged` (`20-wlanap-unmanaged.conf`); firewall zone `nm-shared` |
| P2P device (no netdev) | `P2P-device` | NetworkManager (`p2p-dev-wlan0`, `wifi-p2p`) | `disconnected` |
| `usb0` | Ethernet (USB NCM) | `usb-ncm-dnsmasq@usb0` | `unmanaged` in NetworkManager ([USB networking](network-services.md#usb-networking-and-adb)) |
| `teql0` | | | `unmanaged`, down |

`wlan0` and `wlanap` were both up on the same `phy0`, which the combination rule above permits (`#channels <= 2`).

## NetworkManager and wpa_supplicant

**Tag: Public (upstream)** for the components; **Internal** for the drop-ins.

| Package | Version | State |
|---|---|---|
| `networkmanager` | 1.52.1-1.5 | active; `nmcli -t general` printed `connected:full:enabled:enabled:missing:enabled:no (guessed)` |
| `wpa_supplicant` | 2:2.10-9.3 | active: `/usr/bin/wpa_supplicant -u -s -O /run/wpa_supplicant` (`BusName=fi.w1.wpa_supplicant1`) |
| `iwd` | 3.11-2 | installed, inactive |
| `hostapd` | 2.11-5.3 | not a running unit; `softapmanager` runs `hostapd /var/run/softap_hostapd.conf` |
| `dnsmasq` | 2.92-1 | run by `softapmanager` for `wlanap` and by `usb-ncm-dnsmasq@usb0` for `usb0` |
| `iw` | 6.17-1 | |

NetworkManager drop-ins:

| File | Owner | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `/usr/lib/NetworkManager/conf.d/10-steamos-defaults.conf` | `steamos-customizations-deckard` | `dns=systemd-resolved`, `iwd-config-path=auto`, `ipv6.ip6-privacy=2`. The `wifi.backend=iwd` lines are commented out under "deckard: not turning this on until we switch to iwd". |
| `/usr/lib/NetworkManager/conf.d/20-connectivity.conf` | `networkmanager` | connectivity check `uri=http://ping.archlinux.org/nm-check.txt` |
| `/usr/lib/NetworkManager/conf.d/20-wlanap-unmanaged.conf` | `steamos-customizations-deckard` | "Tell NetworkManager to not manage wlanap from softapmanager": `unmanaged-devices=interface-name:wlanap` |
| `/usr/lib/NetworkManager/conf.d/30-wifi-no-power-save.conf` | `steamos-customizations-deckard` | "Disable power saving on wifi connections": `wifi.powersave = 2` |
| `/etc/NetworkManager/conf.d/99-valve-wifi-backend.conf` | unowned | `wifi.powersave=2`, `wifi.backend=wpa_supplicant` |

The `99-valve-wifi-backend.conf` path, the keys `wifi.powersave` and `wifi.backend`, and `/etc/systemd/system/iwd.service.d/99-valve-override.conf` appear in `/usr/lib/steamos-manager`'s strings. SteamOS Manager exposes them as `WifiBackend1` and `WifiPowerManagement1` ([D-Bus](dbus.md#wifibackend1-wifipowermanagement1)).

## Bluetooth controller

**Tag: Public (upstream)** for the stack (BlueZ 5.79-1.6); **Internal** for the board wiring.

| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Transport | UART: `/soc@0/geniqup@8c0000/serial@898000/bluetooth`, compatible `qcom,wcn7850-bt` | `/sys/class/bluetooth/hci0/device/uevent` |
| Driver | `hci_uart_qca` | same |
| Firmware | `qca/hmtbtfw20.tlv`, `qca/hmtnv20.bin` | [Firmware → Bluetooth](firmware.md#bluetooth) |
| Address | set from the EEPROM at boot by `set-bluetooth-mac-address.service` | [services](services.md#hardware-and-power) |
| `rfkill` | `rfkill0`, type `bluetooth`, `hci0`, unblocked | `/sys/class/rfkill/` |

`bluetoothctl show` (address and name removed):

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `Manufacturer` | `0x001d (29)` |
| `Version` | `0x0d (13)` |
| `Class` | `0x006c0000` |
| `Powered` / `Discoverable` / `Pairable` | `yes` / `no` / `yes` |

| `Modalias` | `usb:v1D6Bp0246d054F` |
| Advertising | 16 instances; secondary channels `1M`, `2M`, `Coded`; TX power −32 to 11; max advertising and scan response length 251; `CanSetTxPower`, `HardwareOffload` |

BlueZ config (`/etc/bluetooth/`, all owned by `bluez`): `main.conf` sets `MultiProfile = multiple`, `FastConnectable = true`, `Privacy = device`, `KernelExperimental = 15c0a148-c273-11ea-b3de-0242ac130004`, and `[LE] ScanIntervalSuspend=2240`, `ScanWindowSuspend=224`. `wake-policy.conf` has a `[WakeAllowed]` section with every device class (`Computer`, `Phone`, `LAN/Network`, `Audio/Video`, `Imaging`, `Wearable`, `Toy`, `Health`, `Uncategorized`) set to `false`. `input.conf` and `network.conf` contain only `[General]`. The `bluetooth.service` unit has no drop-ins.

The controllers don't use this Bluetooth controller; they go through a separate nRF52 radio ([Controllers → How they connect](controllers.md#how-they-connect)).

## Bluetooth audio

**Tag: Public (upstream).** PipeWire's BlueZ plugin directory `/usr/lib/spa-0.2/bluez5/` has codec modules for SBC, AAC, aptX, LDAC, LC3, Opus, Opus-G, FastStream, G.722, and HFP CVSD, mSBC, LC3-SWB and LC3-A127. The codec libraries `sbc`, `libfdk-aac`, `libfreeaptx`, `libldac` and `liblc3` are installed. WirePlumber's settings on the headset surveyed: `bluetooth.profile-preference` `quality`, `bluetooth.autoswitch-to-headset-profile` `true`, `bluetooth.use-persistent-storage` `true`; `20-bluetooth.conf` disables `monitor.bluez-midi`. Which codec headphones negotiate wasn't observed.

`microphone-tracker.lua` sets `echo_cancel_fallback_source` and `echo_cancel_fallback_sink` to disabled when the default sink's name starts with `bluez_output` (comment `-- temporary`). See [Audio → `microphone-tracker.lua`](audio.md#microphone-trackerlua).

## The headset's own access point

**Tag: Internal.** `softapmanager` (root, package `softapmanager` 1.2.37-1) runs the access point on `wlanap`. Its control socket, commands, search plan and the `hbs`/`hbs6`/`scs` modes are on [Local sockets and IPC → Soft-AP manager](local-ipc.md#soft-ap-manager); its ports are on [network services](network-services.md#the-frames-own-wi-fi-hotspot).

- **Processes.** `hostapd /var/run/softap_hostapd.conf` (root) and `dnsmasq -k -x /var/run/softap_dnsmasq.pid -C /var/run/softap_dnsmasq.conf … --log-facility /var/log/dnsmasq_ap.log --log-debug` (as `nobody`). The generated config files contain the network name and password and weren't read.
- **Steam's side.** `steamclient.so` opens `/var/run/softapmanager.socket` itself (strings `Error: can't open softapmanager socket`, `softapmanager is replying again`) and contains the commands `get-plan`, `teardown`, `streamon`, `streamoff` and `set-fallback-country-code`. It has a console command, `remote_client_softapcmd <softapcmd args>`, and the classes `CRemoteClientSoftAP` (with `SetPairedSSIDAndPassword`, `UpdateStreamingMode`, `YieldingConnectWithFallbacks`) and `CRemoteClientPairWifiAP` (log `CRemoteClientPairWifiAPResponse sent ssid %s`).
- **The streaming socket.** `vrlink` and `vrlinkquery` (below) both contain the path `/var/run/softapmanager.streaming.socket` ([Local sockets and IPC → Streaming socket](local-ipc.md#streaming-socket)). Next to it in `vrlink` are `streamon`, `streamoff`, `Could not open streaming scan suppression socket` and `Streaming scan suppression socket went down.`
- **After resume** the sleep hook runs `softapcmd delayrefresh` ([power](power.md#system-sleep-hooks)).

## PC streaming: `vrlink`

**Tag: Internal.** Everything here is from files and strings. `vrlink` wasn't running during the survey, and no streaming session was observed.

### Files

`/opt/steamvr/tools/vrlink/` (part of `deckard-steamvr-rel`):

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `bin/linuxarm64/vrlink` | The client (2.5 MB) |
| `bin/linuxarm64/vrlinkquery` | A query tool (0.7 MB) |
| `bin/linuxarm64/run_vrlink.sh` | Sets `TU_DEBUG=gmem` if unset, `VRLINK_SAVE_VIDEO_DATA=0` and `VRLINK_SUBMIT_DELAY_US=6000`, runs `./vrlink "$@"` as a child and forwards `TERM`, `INT`, `HUP` and `QUIT` to it |
| `bin/linuxarm64/run_vrlink_udp.sh` | `./run_vrlink.sh -c "$@"`; its usage line is `./run_vrlink_udp.sh <pc-ip>` (an example address in the original) |
| `bin/linuxarm64/run_vrlink_renderdoc.sh` | Runs `vrlink` with `LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/librenderdoc.so` |
| `bin/linuxarm64/run_vrlinkquery.sh` | Runs `vrlinkquery` |
| `resources/` | Shaders (`eye`, `statusshader`, `warpwindowpreview`), icons, `legacy_manifest.json` with default bindings for `knuckles` and `frame_controller` |

`steamclient.so` contains `/tools/vrlink/bin/linuxarm64/run_vrlink.sh`, the option `-vrlinkforceenable`, `k_EVRLinkCapsAvailable`, `k_EVRLinkCapsUnimplemented`, `k_EVRLinkCapsUnknown` and `k_EVRLinkCapsMissingHardwareEncoding`. A polkit action names `/opt/steamvr/tools/vrlink/bin/linuxarm64/stream_mode.sh`, which doesn't exist ([permissions](permissions.md#polkit-what-runs-as-root-without-a-password)).

### What the client's strings show

- **Options:** `-b bind UDP (server)`, `-c <IP> connect to UDP at the IP address`, `-d <device> Control which device the local UDP port is bound to`, `-e steam string`, `-n paired link access point network to be active with "vrlink connect"`, `-f <FILENAME> specify DataLink filename`, `-h Hide Client Debug UI`.
- **Transport:** classes `SVLDataLinkUDP`, `SVLDataLinkTransferUDP` and `SVLDataLinkUber` (`Found primary link %s`, `AddAndInitLinkTransfer %s / PEERED: %s`), `SO_BINDTODEVICE`, IPv6 support, and AES routines (`EVP_aes_128_cbc`, `Key setup failure in transport subsystem`). It also contains the strings `foxnet`, `usb` and `enx`. (`foxnet` is also the name of a `/persist` config key; see [SteamVR on the Frame → Per-device config in `/persist`](steamvr.md#per-device-config-in-persist).)
- **Video decode:** `SVLCodecV4L2` runs the decoder through V4L2 (`V4L2_EVENT_SOURCE_CHANGE`, `DISPLAY_DELAY`, `> 300ms between our last forward progress. Asking remote side for a new IFrame`). It finds the device with `vrdevice_path video_decode`, which resolves to `/dev/video22` ([Hardware access → `vrdevice_path`: the name-to-node map](hardware.md#vrdevice_path-the-name-to-node-map)). A debug string names `test.h265`.
- **Audio:** `SVLClientAudio` connects to PipeWire (`Failed to connect to pipewire. Is pipewire running and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR correct?`) and also has PulseAudio code paths.
- `vrserver` contains `VRLink client disconnected`, `driver_vrlink`, `vrlink.client` and settings such as `/vrlink/steamvr/remoteClientRefreshRate` and `/vrlink/steamvr/remote_roomview_enabled`. `/opt/steamvr/drivers/` on the headset has no `vrlink` driver.

### Hardware codec formats

`v4l2-ctl --list-formats-out` / `--list-formats` (query only):

| Node | Compressed side | Raw side |
|---|---|---|
| `/dev/video22` (decoder, `/dev/video-dec0`) | input: `H264`, `HEVC`, `VP90` | output: `Q08C`, `NV12`, `NV21`, `AB24`, `QC24` |
| `/dev/video23` (encoder, `/dev/video-enc0`) | output: `H264`, `HEVC` | input: `Q08C`, `NV12`, `NV21`, `AB24`, `QC24` |

The codec block and its firmware are on [Firmware → Video codec](firmware.md#video-codec). `steamwebhelper` holds `/dev/video22` open during a normal session ([Hardware access → Cameras](hardware.md#cameras)).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    accTitle: Wireless and PC streaming components on the headset
    accDescr: NetworkManager with wpa_supplicant runs the client connection on wlan0. softapmanager runs hostapd and dnsmasq for the access point on wlanap. Both interfaces are on phy0, the WCN7850 driven by ath12k. The Steam client sends commands to softapmanager over /var/run/softapmanager.socket, and its strings name vrlink's run_vrlink.sh. vrlink's strings name the soft-AP streaming socket with streamon and streamoff, a UDP link to a PC, and the hardware decoder found through vrdevice_path video_decode, which is /dev/video22. A vrlink session was not observed, and the PC side was not examined.
    NM["NetworkManager +<br/>wpa_supplicant"] --> W0["wlan0 (client)"]
    SAM["softapmanager (root)"] --> HAP["hostapd + dnsmasq"]
    HAP --> WAP["wlanap (AP)"]
    W0 --> PHY["phy0: WCN7850, ath12k"]
    WAP --> PHY
    SC["Steam client<br/>(steamclient.so)"] -->|"softapmanager.socket:<br/>get-plan, teardown,<br/>streamon/off, fallback country"| SAM
    SC ---|"names run_vrlink.sh"| VRL["vrlink"]
    VRL ---|"named in strings:<br/>streaming socket,<br/>streamon / streamoff"| SAM
    VRL ---|"vrdevice_path video_decode"| DEC["/dev/video22<br/>H.264, HEVC, VP9 decode"]
    VRL -.->|"UDP link; not observed"| PC["PC (not examined)"]
```

## Interpretation

*This section is interpretation, not observation. It combines the facts above with general knowledge and may be wrong.*

- **A dongle-to-headset link.** The `ath12k.conf` comments speak of streams "from the dongle -> HMD" with retries "restricted severely", and of tagging vrlink packets as video. Together with the soft AP's hidden-SSID `hbs6` plan and the 320 MHz AP capability in 6 GHz, this suggests a PC-side Wi-Fi dongle joins the headset's own access point, so the headset is the AP and the PC is a client.
- **Scan suppression during streaming.** `vrlink` calls the streaming socket its "scan suppression socket", and `softapmanager` references `cfg80211_block_scans`. Background Wi-Fi scans briefly take the radio off-channel, which would cause latency spikes in a stream. Blocking them while streaming would avoid that.
- **The Bluetooth numbers.** In the Bluetooth assigned numbers, company ID 29 (`0x001d`) is Qualcomm and HCI version 13 (`0x0d`) is Core 5.4. Modalias vendor `0x1d6b` is the Linux Foundation, which BlueZ uses for its own device ID.
- **HEVC is the likely stream codec.** The decoder accepts H.264, HEVC and VP9, the encoder H.264 and HEVC, and the only file name in `vrlink` is `test.h265`. HEVC is a reasonable guess for the stream, but it wasn't observed.

## How to inspect this yourself

All read-only. Don't run `iw scan`, `iw … set`, `nmcli … connect`/`modify`, `bluetoothctl scan|pair|connect|power|discoverable`, `softapcmd create|teardown|refresh`, or `vrlink` itself.

```sh
iw dev                      # prints MAC addresses and network names; redact before sharing
iw phy | less
iw reg get                  # reveals your regulatory country
nmcli -t general; nmcli device
bluetoothctl list; bluetoothctl show   # print the controller address and host name
grep . /sys/class/rfkill/rfkill*/{type,name,soft,hard}
lspci -s 01:00.0; modinfo -p ath12k; cat /usr/lib/modprobe.d/ath12k.conf
grep -r . /usr/lib/NetworkManager/conf.d/ /etc/NetworkManager/conf.d/
ls /usr/lib/spa-0.2/bluez5/
ls -lR /opt/steamvr/tools/vrlink
strings -n 4 /opt/steamvr/tools/vrlink/bin/linuxarm64/vrlink | grep -E '^-[a-z] |softapmanager|vrdevice_path'
v4l2-ctl -d /dev/video22 --list-formats-out; v4l2-ctl -d /dev/video23 --list-formats
```

Don't read `/var/run/softap_hostapd.conf`, `/var/run/softap_dnsmasq.conf` or `/etc/NetworkManager/system-connections/` into anything you share; they hold network names and passwords.

## Not determined

- Where `ieee80211_regdom` gets its value at boot, and how Steam's IP-country lookup and `set-fallback-country-code` interact with it
- How `vrlink` uses the streaming socket in practice: when it sends `streamon`/`streamoff`, and what `softapmanager` changes in response
- Which Wi-Fi network a streaming session uses (the client link on `wlan0`, the access point on `wlanap`, or USB), and what the `-n` option's "paired link access point network" is
- Which video codec a PC stream uses; only the decoder's supported formats were read
- What `foxnet` refers to
- What the `egap` and `gtx` driver options do beyond their descriptions
- Which Bluetooth codec is negotiated with headphones, and whether LE Audio is used
